title: When Road Hazard Protection Coverage Starts
content:
Coverage under a Road Hazard Protection certificate starts when the covered tires go on the vehicle, never on the sale date. Until then the certificate is pending.

**Activation.** The certificate must be in status pending when it is activated. On activation:
- the effective date is the covered set's install date;
- the expiration date is the effective date plus the plan term, counted as calendar months to the same day of the month, falling back to the last day of that month when that day does not exist;
- for the Life-of-Tread plan, coverage also ends earlier for any tire whose tread reaches the plan's coverage tread limit;
- a plan whose roadside calls per term are above zero is credited that many roadside calls in one allowance entry; a plan with zero is credited nothing.

Unused roadside calls never carry past the term.

**Expiration-date examples (hypothetical install dates).**

| Install date | Plan term | Expiration date |
|---|---|---|
| March 15 | 12 months | March 15 of the following year |
| August 31 | 6 months (illustrative term) | the last day of February |
| January 31 | 24 months | January 31 two years later |

**Roadside allowance on activation.**

| Plan | Calls credited at activation |
|---|---|
| Plus 36-Month, Life-of-Tread, Commercial LT | the plan's roadside calls per term, in one allowance entry |
| 12-Month, 24-Month, 36-Month | nothing |
